steps.question: Pau wrote down five lunch prices at Gonzaga (₱): 65, 70, 75, 80, 410. Someone bought a party tray. Which average best describes a typical lunch?

options.whyWrong: The mean is (65 + 70 + 75 + 80 + 410) ÷ 5 = ₱140, which is more than four of the five lunches. The outlier 410 pulls it up.
No price appears more than once, so this data set has no mode.
The range (410 − 65 = 345) measures spread, not the center. It tells you how far apart the prices are, not what a typical lunch costs.

steps.hint: One price is far from the rest. Which average does one extreme value pull the most?

polya.understand: You want one number for a typical lunch. One value, 410, is an outlier.
polya.plan: Find the mean and the median, then see which one is closer to most of the prices.
polya.lookBack: Mean = 700 ÷ 5 = 140; median = 75 (the middle value when sorted). Four of the five prices are near 75.

steps.explanation: The median is the middle value of the sorted data: 65, 70, 75, 80, 410, so it's ₱75. The mean, ₱140, uses every value, so the outlier 410 drags it up above almost every lunch. The mean is sensitive to extreme values; the median and mode are not.
steps.why: Reports about incomes and prices often use the median for exactly this reason: a few very large values can make the mean misleading.

steps.question: Zach timed orders (in seconds) at three Gonzaga stalls. All three have a mean of 35. Which statement is true?

options.text: Stall C is the most spread out: range 50
All three are the same, since the means match
options.whyWrong: The averages match, but the data don't. Stall A never varies, while Stall C goes from 10 to 60 seconds.

options.text: Stall A is the most spread out
options.whyWrong: Every value in A is 35, so its range, standard deviation, and variance are all 0. It has no spread at all.

options.text: Stall B has the biggest range
options.whyWrong: B's range is 45 − 25 = 20. C's range is 60 − 10 = 50, so C is more spread out.

steps.hint: Range = highest value − lowest value. Work it out for each stall.

polya.understand: The three stalls have the same mean, 35. The question is about how spread out the times are.
polya.plan: Find each stall's range: highest minus lowest.
polya.lookBack: Ranges: A = 0, B = 20, C = 50. The standard deviations agree: 0, about 6.32, and about 17.03.

steps.explanation: A measure of center alone can't tell these stalls apart: all three have mean and median 35. Measures of dispersion can. The ranges are 0, 20, and 50, and the standard deviations are 0, about 6.32, and about 17.03, so Stall C's times are the most spread out.
steps.why: Two stalls with the same average wait can feel very different. Knowing the spread tells you how much you can trust the average.
